_why: Two separate sets. the examples, in leanring-buddy/QuestionKindExamples.json, are what the sorters that learn from examples get to see; 'test' is what every sorter is graded on. None of the test phrasings appear in the examples, and the keyword lists in CompanionManager.swift were written before this file, so no sorter was tuned to the test. Phrasings are written the way Apple Speech transcribes them: lowercase, no punctuation, spoken filler kept. Every test item is mid-conversation, after an answer about the off-by-one bug on the URL-shortener screen.
previous_answer: the crash starts here. high is set to the length, so it points one past the last real index, and with the loop condition using less than or equal, low can climb until mid lands exactly on that out of range slot.

kinds.quick: a small specific question with a one sentence answer, like what a line does or what a term means
kinds.normal: a real question about how or why something works, wanting a short explanation
kinds.teach: asking to be taught something properly, a walk-through or a deeper full explanation
kinds.reexplain: saying the last explanation did not land and asking for it again or differently
kinds.tradeoff: asking for a judgement between options or designs, whether something is better or worth it
